RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the December 16, 2008/Agrahayana 25, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Prime Minister; Ministries : Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture;
Finance; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
70
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Comparison of inflation rate with
international trend
*201. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) how does the inflation rate for
cereals,  pulses and edible oils in India
compare with the international trends; and
(b) what is the impact of international
price behaviour on national price trends in
respect of aforesaid commodities?
Incentives to aviation industries
*202. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether after handing out a slew of
incentives to the aviation industry, over
the past two months, a Committee of
Secretaries led by Cabinet Secretary
considered in a schedule of meetings to
assess the impact of the measures on the
sector and the need for additional measures
to be taken; and
(b) if so, what are the main subjects
discussed and what are the proposals
prepared and to what extent they have
agreed to improve the aviation industry?
Abolition of Travel Agency
commission
*203. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT
: Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware
of the fact that some airlines have declared
abolition of Travel Agency commission and
have advised to earn their income by
charging the clients additional fees ranging
from Rs. 350/- to Rs. 10,000/- over and
above the ticket fares, which would be an
additional burden to the public;
(b) if so, the details of airlines and the
reasons for such abolition; and
(c) the measures taken by Government
to correct the situation?
Effect of terrorism on tourism
†*204. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased
to state:

71
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(a) whether given terror activities,
tourism has been affected;
(b) if so, the extent thereof; and
(c) the new dimension added to tourism
over past four years with names of the
new spots identified?
Proposal for development of tourism
in Kerala
*205. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased
to state:
(a) whether proposals for tourism
development have been received from the
State of Kerala;
(b) if so, the details of the proposals
received along with the funds required;
(c) whether necessary clearances have
been granted to the projects submitted by
the State;
(d) if so, the details of the projects
clearance granted and the projects still
pending for clearance; and
(e) the funds so far released against each
project?
Heritage status to Varanasi Ghats and
Sarnath Bodh Stupas
†*206. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
include 'ghats' of V aranasi and Bodh Stupas
situated at Sarnath in the heritage sites; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken in this regard?
Manipulations in stock markets
*207. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the scale of volatility
witnessed in the Indian stock market since
early this year is unprecedented;
(b) if not, how Government viewed it;
(c) the steps taken by Government for
ensuring prudent conduct of the market
player and for detection of market
manipulations indicating results yielded, if
any, by such steps;
(d) whether despite strong view
expressed by the Security and Exchange
Board of India (SEBI) against lending of
stocks by Foreign Financial Institutions to
their clients overseas, Foreign Institutional
Investors (FIIs) continued to indulge in it;
and
(e) if so, the reasons for not banning the
same?
Protection of Indian tourism
industry
*208. SHRI NARESH GUJRAL: Will
the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to
state:
(a) what steps Government is taking to
protect the Indian tourism industry from
the global meltdown; and
(b) what is the expected increase/
decrease of tourist arrivals in the current
year, given the present economic
scenario?

72
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Jobs for disabled persons in the
private sector
*209. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
SHRI R.C. SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a plan was
announced during the last Budget Speech
to employ one lakh disabled persons in
private sector in the current financial year;
(b) if so, the details of the plan;
(c) whether it is a fact that not a single
appointment has been made so far under
this scheme; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and what
corrective measures are being taken in this
regard?
Small savings schemes offered by Post
Offices
*210. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the small savings schemes
offered through Post Offices have fallen out
of favour with the investors and seen massive
withdrawals during the past few years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has since taken
any corrective steps to ensure investors'
interest in Post Office small savings
schemes and also bring it at par with the
banking sector; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Price of petrol and diesel
†*211. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI SHIV ANAND TIWARI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the attention of
Government has been drawn towards some
media reports wherein likely prices of
petrol and diesel in India have been shown,
post reduction in the price of crude in
international market;
(b) if so, these prices of petrol and diesel
separately; and
(c) the extent to which these prices are
less than the prices being charged from
consumers of petrol and diesel in the
country currently?
Overseas loans for domestic
infrastructure companies
*212. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
make it easy for the domestic infrastructure
companies to raise foreign funds for various
infrastructure projects;
(b) the names of the companies, which
have obtained overseas loans during the last
three years, separately alongwith the names
of the funding agencies and the names of
the banks where these funds have been
parked; and
(c) the amount of funds withdrawn
by each of these companies till date and
the steps taken by Government to ensure
the utilization of these funds for the
projects for which these funds have been
obtained?

73
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Pay revision of bank employees
*213. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state the reason for not
finalizing the pay revision of Nationalized
Banks, State Bank of India, Reserve Bank
of India, Scheduled Commercial Banks,
General Insurance Corporation, Life
Insurance Corporation officers and
employees and by when the pay revision
of these employees would be completed?
Modernisation of Kolkata airport
*214. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether some political parties have
written to the Prime Minister with reference
to its policies on modernisation of Kolkata
and 35 other non-metro airports in the
country;
(b) if so, whether some of the parties
have questioned Government's decision in
this regard;
(c) if so, what are the main reasons put
forward for reversing policy of
modernisation of Kolkata and other 35 non-
metro airports in the country; and
(d) what is the final decision taken and
whether Government has agreed to
modernise these airports also?
Share of Rajasthan in profit from
petroleum products
†*215. DR. PRABHA THAKUR : Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the places in Rajasthan where the
work of exploration and production of
petroleum products is likely to be started
along with the details thereof; and
(b) the quantum of share for the State
ensured by Central Government out of the
profit earned from the production of
petroleum products in Rajasthan?
International crude prices vis-a-vis
domestic petrol price
†*216. SHRI SHIVANAND TIWARI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the price of
crude in the international market had come
down to 45.50 Dollar per Barrel in the past
few days;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the price of crude oil in the
international market at the time when the
prices of petrol, diesel and cooking gas were
last increased in the past months in the
country; and
(d) the months and years during which
crude prices ranged between 45 to 50 Dollar
per Barrel in the international market?
Moderation in revenue growth
*217. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRIMA TI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Empowered Committee of
the State Finance Ministers have expressed
apprehension that the global financial
meltdown can lead to a moderation in
revenue growth;

74
(b) if so, whether the Committee during
its meeting decided on a number of measures
to be taken;
(c) if so, what are the main
recommendations made by the Committee
and to what extent Government has agreed
to implement their suggestions; and
(d) whether any final decision for
implementation has been considered?
Merger of posts
*218. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to refer
to answer to Unstarred Question 369 given
in the Rajya Sabha on 21st October, 2008
and state:
(a) the date from which the merger of
posts in the pre-revised scales of Rs. 6500-
10500 and Rs. 7450-11500 has been made
effective;
(b) the details of the posts so merged,
Ministry-wise and Department-wise;
(c) the details of the procedure followed
to decide the inter-se seniority of the cadre
after the merger of the posts; and
(d) if no such directions have been
issued, the reasons therefor?
Air Turbine Fuel under declared
goods category
*219. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is considering
any proposal to declare the Air Turbine
Fuel (ATF) under declared goods category;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when decision is likely to be
taken by Government in this regard?
New runway at IGI Airport, Delhi
*220. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the new runway at Indira
Gandhi International (IGI) Airport was
opened for commercial operations recently;
(b) if so, whether the runway has been
plagued with teething troubles such as snag
in ILS and poor lighting systems;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether Government proposes to
take immediate steps to remove all such
snags at the new runway of IGI Airport so
that passengers can enjoy congestion free
landing at the airport?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 10th December, 2008 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 19, 1930 (Saka)

I N D E X
